card.trust_empty_town_hall.text: Your Aide counts thirty-two staff members, nine reporters, and eleven residents in a hall prepared for six hundred. "People saw the invitation. They simply decided that an evening with us was not worth leaving home for."
card.trust_empty_town_hall.left: Cancel the stage and pay for small neighborhood meetings where people can question you directly.
card.trust_empty_town_hall.right: Fill the front rows with paid organizers and film the room from a tighter angle.
card.trust_volunteer_wave.text: The Family Representative shows you a map covered in handwritten names. Hundreds of residents have offered cars, spare rooms, food, and evenings of unpaid work. No party office recruited them. They came because their neighbors asked.
card.trust_volunteer_wave.left: Let the local groups keep control and use their network to reach neglected districts.
card.trust_volunteer_wave.right: Put the volunteers under your campaign brand and sell sponsors access to the movement.
card.trust_polling_bubble.text: The Press Officer places two charts side by side. The public poll says you are admired. Complaints, empty meetings, and private interviews say something else. "We can commission an honest sample—or release the flattering number before anyone asks how it was made."
card.trust_polling_bubble.left: Pay for independent polling and let the public number move toward the truth.
card.trust_polling_bubble.right: Publish the flattering poll and raise money while the headline still holds.
card.trust_quiet_reservoir.text: The Reformist returns from districts your consultants stopped visiting. "The national numbers are wrong. People there trust the work, not the name on the television. They will organize—but only if we do not turn them into scenery."
card.trust_quiet_reservoir.left: Fund open town halls and make the underestimated support visible.
card.trust_quiet_reservoir.right: Keep the network local and let it deepen without a national campaign around it.
card.trust_public_mandate.text: The Reformist lays out a bill that every previous government called impossible. Your office has the votes, and the public is willing to endure the disruption. "This is the rare moment when authority and consent point in the same direction."
card.trust_public_mandate.left: Spend the mandate on an independent reform that will limit your own office too.
card.trust_public_mandate.right: Use the popularity to sell access to the program before support cools.
card.trust_beloved_figurehead.text: The Coalition Whip has an uncomfortable summary. "People believe you. Committees do not obey you. We can lend you a machine by morning, but machines remember who owns them. Or your supporters can build one slowly themselves."
card.trust_beloved_figurehead.left: Fund a grassroots vote operation and let supporters build durable power.
card.trust_beloved_figurehead.right: Take the coalition's money and machinery, along with its future claims.
card.trust_coercive_stability.text: Your Aide brings a list of orders that were acknowledged but never carried out. Local offices comply on paper; residents refuse meetings, witnesses stop answering, and volunteers have vanished. "We still have enough power to hide the refusal—or enough time to admit why it began."
card.trust_coercive_stability.left: Publish the failures, surrender control to an independent review, and pay for restitution.
card.trust_coercive_stability.right: Remove the reports, pressure local media, and announce that implementation is complete.
card.trust_abandoned_office.text: The Family Representative waits in a reception room with no staff and no other visitors. "Nobody expects this office to help anymore. That means the difficult cases are still here—and so are the brokers offering to make the room look powerful again."
card.trust_abandoned_office.left: Take the abandoned cases and rebuild trust one family at a time.
card.trust_abandoned_office.right: Sell privileged access to the empty office and use the money to rebuild its machinery.
